key_insight: A temporal deep learning model using longitudinal OCT scans can forecast both onset of geographic atrophy and progression from non-central to central involvement years in advance.
clinical_relevance: If validated, this approach could help identify dry AMD patients at higher risk for clinically important GA progression and support earlier monitoring or trial enrollment.
method: Encoded OCT B-scans with pretrained ResNet-18, ResNet-50, and ViT-B/16 backbones.
Modeled visit sequences with RNN, LSTM, or Transformer networks, with optional time-gap ({Delta}t) inputs.
Trained separate models for 2- to 6-year prediction horizons using patient-level 80/20 splits and multiple random seeds.
evidence_signal: In 91 patients and 455 OCT volumes, ROC-AUC reached 0.84-0.94 for NGA-to-GA prediction at 2-4 years and up to 0.96 for NCGA-to-CGA prediction at 4-5 years.
watch_item: Single-center retrospective data and small cohort size mean performance may not generalize without external, prospective validation.
paper_title: Sequential Deep Learning to Predict Non-Central to Central Geographic Atrophy Progression from OCT Imaging
